title: FITA — Flexible Image Transfer Alpha: a FITS convention for multi-layer astronomical images
description:
FITA is a FITS convention for multi-layer astronomical images that lets a user balance data so as to re-naturalise sliced and measured phenomena lying beyond the reach of human senses, while maintaining the scientific integrity of the measurements. Calibrated flux is held in FLUX_* extensions and display transparency in paired ALPHA_* extensions, so re-selecting a display range changes only what the eye sees and never the measured flux, verified bit-for-bit. It adds per-layer blend modes, non-destructive adjustment layers, stereo depth encoding physical ISM penetration, and IVOA ObsCore v1.2 provenance, while remaining a valid FITS multi-extension file readable by any FITS reader. Designed for multi-wavelength astronomy and the integration of multispectral measurements into physical models and astrophysical inference, FITA is intended to be multi-wavelength and multidisciplinary, and is at the heart of the MWVO (Multi-Wave Virtual Observatory).

This record contains the format specification, the reference implementation, the fita conform conformance checker, and a labelled conformance corpus of 18 byte-reproducible files against which an independent implementation can be scored.
notes: The software is MIT licensed. The format specification is dedicated to the public domain under CC0 (see LICENSE-SPEC): a specification that cannot be freely re-implemented is not a standard.
